title: Peanut Chicken Rice Bowls
seoTitle: Peanut Chicken Rice Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Saucy chicken, crunchy vegetables, and rice for ten
subtitle: Saucy chicken, crunchy vegetables, and rice for ten
description: Tender chicken, jasmine rice, cabbage, carrots, and peanut sauce make a filling build-your-own bowl.

steps.title: Rinse rice
steps.instruction: Rinse rice until the water is less cloudy, then cook with water in a covered pot.

steps.title: Whisk sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, warm water, and chili sauce until pourable.

steps.title: Cut chicken
steps.instruction: Cut thighs into bite-size pieces so they cook evenly; wash hands and board afterward.

steps.title: Heat pan
steps.instruction: Heat a wide skillet over medium-high until a drop of water sizzles, then add oil.

steps.title: Brown chicken
steps.instruction: Cook chicken in batches without crowding, turning until browned and 165°F in the thickest piece.

steps.title: Cook vegetables
steps.instruction: Stir cabbage and carrots in the hot pan for 3 minutes so they soften but remain crisp.

steps.title: Sauce chicken
steps.instruction: Return chicken to the skillet and toss with half the peanut sauce; loosen with water if it clumps.

steps.title: Fluff rice
steps.instruction: Rest cooked rice covered for 5 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork.

steps.title: Check heat
steps.instruction: Hold chicken above 140°F and keep cold toppings below 40°F until the meal break.

steps.title: Build bowls
steps.instruction: Spoon rice into bowls, add sauced chicken and vegetables, then drizzle remaining sauce.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Chicken thighs — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Chicken thighs and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Thin peanut sauce with hot water, not oil.
Keep lime wedges separate for bright flavour.
Use sunflower butter for a peanut-free crew.
tonightSpread: Condiments: lime wedges, chili crisp, crushed peanuts
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Chicken thighs in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Turn leftovers into cold noodle salad.
whyCrewsLikeIt: The sauce can be made ahead and the toppings hold well for staggered dinner breaks.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: cook rice and sauce up to 2 days ahead. Storage: refrigerate components separately for 3 days. Reheating: heat chicken to 165°F before serving.
substitutions: Use tofu or chickpeas for chicken.
Use brown rice or cauliflower rice.
